name: Dusty coral
lede: Dusty coral is a warm, muted orange-pink, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Akako-iro, "red incense colored," named for scented wood rather than the reef animal its English name suggests.

sections.title: The color of red incense wood
sections.body:
Akako-iro (赤香色) is named in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors for "red incense-colored," not for coral, the reef animal whose skeleton gives the English name here [1]. The page gives no further history for the name beyond that literal meaning, and it is undocumented in the sources consulted here [1].

Its nearest named neighbor on file is [[dark-peach]], 3.3 units off [2]; [[pinkish-orange]] sits 3.8 off and the everyday name [[coral]] itself is 4.0 off, close enough to blur together on screen despite the different sources.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within six units of this swatch in only 33 of 23,781 paintings, 0.14 percent, as photographed; looking inside each painting for at least five percent coverage narrows that to 29 [3]. That makes it rarer than 57 percent of the named colors in our library [3]. It peaks in the 1500s, present in 0.4 percent of our 2,231 paintings from that century, 2.4 times the museums' baseline rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 86 percent of its 29 appearances by lightness rank [3].

The earliest match, Bernardo Daddi's work, dates to 1333, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [3].
